title: Countermeasure Lattice for Quantization-Induced Drift
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:
This document defines the Countermeasure Lattice: a prioritized, multi-layer catalogue of detection signals and automated/manual mitigations for regressions that appear to be caused or amplified by quantization (including mixed-precision and adaptive per-layer quant). It is intended for model-owners, runtime engineers, SREs, and evaluation teams who manage shadow, canary, and production rollouts.

Why this exists:
- Quantization reduces compute and memory cost but can change fine-grained output distributions, creating subtle drift in coherence, function-call structure, or token probabilities for safety-sensitive prompts.
- Existing eval gates catch many failures, but quantization failures often show as increased variance on targeted slices rather than gross accuracy drops. The lattice provides a graded response plan so we preserve availability while regaining quality.

Intended audience:
- Model onboarding engineers
- Serving runtime owners
- Evaluation and QA teams
- Incident responders for model regressions

Scope and definitions:
- Quantization: any offline or online transformation that reduces numeric precision (e.g., int8, int4, hybrid FP16-int8).
- Drift: measurable degradation on a pre-specified slice or metric relative to a baseline (baseline might be float16 or previously certified quant profile).
- Countermeasure Lattice: layered mitigations from least to most disruptive, with observable preconditions and rollback triggers for each layer.

Detection Signals (examples):
1) Delta-anchored fidelity: per-slice normalized metric change > drift_threshold (see table).
2) Latent syntactic drift: function-call field omission or argument truncation frequency increase > 2x baseline.
3) Embedding cosine contraction: mean cosine to seed-set drops by > 0.03 on critical slices.
4) Token-probability entropy shift: average per-token entropy increases by > 0.2 nats on interactive flows.

Operational thresholds (tunable):
| Metric                          | Baseline window | Warning threshold | Action threshold |
|--------------------------------|-----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Slice F1 (critical intents)    | last 14d        | -3%               | -7%              |
| Functioncall omission rate     | last 30d        | 1.5x              | 2.5x             |
| Embedding mean cosine          | last 30d        | -0.02             | -0.05            |
| Response entropy (nats/token)  | last 7d         | +0.1              | +0.25            |

Countermeasure Lattice (ordered by non-disruptiveness):
Layer A — Localized inference knobs (auto, non-disruptive):
- A1: Adjust runtime quantization temperature heuristic (example CLI):
  - rwmctl set quant.temp-heuristic service=my-service value=0.9
  - Rationale: small shifts in scaling can restore token probability shape without reloading models.
- A2: Enable prefix-level KV cache bypass for high-sensitivity slices for N=1 requests.
- A3: Narrow the batching window for affected route to reduce cross-request smoothing.

Layer B — Prompt and input-level hedges (low disruption):
- B1: Apply targeted priming templates that stabilize response anchors for flagged slices.
- B2: Insert sentinel tokens or function-call prompting scaffolds when function-call omission risk is high. Example rewrite: 'You must return valid JSON with fields...'
- B3: Temporarily increase top-p sampling floor (top_p -> top_p -0.05 but not below 0.6) for the problematic route.

Layer C — Shadow and canary adjustments (moderate disruption):
- C1: Shift affected traffic to a hybrid shadow with float16 baseline and quantized candidate in parallel; compute divergence score and route only when divergence < action threshold.
- C2: Narrow canary cohort to 0.5% of traffic, increase monitoring frequency to 30s.
- C3: Raise evaluator fidelity (increase probe replication by 5x) for the slice.

Layer D — Quant rollback & progressive fallback (high disruption):
- D1: Automated rollback of quant profile for the offending model-service (use feature flag):
  - curl -XPOST https://ops-api/set-profile -d '{"service":"svc","model":"x","profile":"float16"}'
- D2: Deploy mixed-precision hotpatch: keep most layers quantized, de-quantize top-2 transformer blocks.
- D3: Route to ensemble fallback: primary quantized + secondary float16 reranker (costly but preserves UX).

Layer E — Remediation and upgrade (highest disruption):
- E1: Re-run quant synthesis with augmented probe set including failing slice; generate new candidate profiles.
- E2: Full re-quant with layer-wise calibration, extended ADMM-style solver, and increased calibration set size.
- E3: Hold release & schedule model-retrain if root cause correlates to dataset distribution shift.

Automated Decision Rules (recommended):
- If Warning threshold crossed: alert evaluation owners, run A-layer mitigations automatically (A1,A2,A3) and increase probe frequency x2.
- If Action threshold crossed for a single slice and matches known quant-failure fingerprint: enact C1 and notify SREs.
- If Action threshold crossed across >3 independent slices or user-visible defects increase >1%: initiate D1 (rollback) and start E2 remediation.

Playbook: Incident response checklist (short form):
1) Triage (owner: eval-oncall) — confirm signal, gather reproducer probes, capture token-level logs and KV-cache status.
2) Immediate soft mitigations (owner: runtime-oncall): apply A-layer knobs; confirm whether metric returns to warning range within 10 minutes.
3) Canary/Shadow (owner: model-owner): start hybrid shadow per C1 and monitor divergence over next 30 minutes.
4) Decision (owner: platform-lead): if divergence persists, schedule D1 rollback and notify stakeholders; if fixed, draft follow-up and close.
5) Post-incident (owner: applied-ml): run E1/E2 with augmented probe set, publish quant-cert stamp before re-rollout.

Checklist for creating a quant-aware probe set (for E1):
- Include 3x examples from each failing slice, plus adversarial perturbations (synonym swaps, code-style variations).
- Add 50 control examples from baseline to stabilize estimator variance.
- Label expected outputs or invariants (functioncalls, required fields).
- Test across sampling seeds (min 5) and at production prompting temperature settings.

Example JSON gate config (used by eval scheduler):
{
  "service": "conversational-qa",
  "slice_id": "billing-intent",
  "metrics": [
    {"name":"slice_f1","baseline_window":"14d","warning_delta":-0.03,"action_delta":-0.07}
  ],
  "automations": {"on_warning": ["A1","A3"], "on_action": ["C1","D1"]}
}

Cost and SLO considerations:
- Rolling back to float16 increases per-token cost approx +2.0x; mixed-precision hotpatches typically +1.15–1.5x. Balance cost vs. user-impact using the cost-impact matrix below.
| Mitigation                     | Relative cost | Latency impact | Expected quality delta |
|-------------------------------|---------------|----------------|------------------------|
| A-layer knobs                 | 1.00          | 0%             | +small                |
| B-layer prompt hedges         | 1.01          | 0–2%           | +small                |
| C-layer hybrid shadow         | 1.10 (shadow) | +1–5%          | +moderate             |
| D1 rollback (float16)        | 2.0           | +20–50%        | +large                |

Instrumentation and telemetry requirements (minimum):
- Token-level logging for failing requests with redaction for PII.
- Per-slice metric dashboards with 1m resolution and alerting to #eval-ops.
- Drift provenance: store quant-profile id, seed, calibration sample id, and runtime kernel version with each inference trace.

Ownership matrix:
- Detection & probes: Applied-ML (primary), Runtime (secondary)
- Runtime knobs (A-layer): Serving Runtime Team (primary)
- Prompt hedges and probe augmentation: Model Owners / Eval Stewards
- Canary/Shadow orchestration: Platform / SRE
- Rollback & release gating: Release Eng (Platform)

Runbook annex: quick commands and play actions
- Trigger a float16 rollback (dry-run):
  - opsctl profile apply --service conversational-qa --profile float16 --dry-run
- Force increased probe replication for a slice:
  - evalctl replicate --slice billing-intent --factor 5 --duration 2h
- Start hybrid-shadow with replay:
  - shadowctl start --service svc --baseline-profile float16 --candidate-profile int8 --cohort 0.5% --metrics divergence_score

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- For every quant-related incident, create a short postmortem with: root cause hypothesis, countermeasure applied, time-to-detect, time-to-restore, and quant-cert stamp change.
- Maintain a quarterly "quant-safety" retro that samples closed incidents, extracts recurring failure modes, and updates the lattice with new mitigations.

Appendix A — Failure fingerprints (examples):
- Fingerprint: "Top-layer coherence loss" — symptom: increased sentence-level repetition after 20+ tokens; signature: rising token entropy localized to last 10 tokens.
- Fingerprint: "Functioncall truncation" — symptom: output missing required JSON fields; signature: increased occurrence of truncated braces or early EOS token.

Appendix B — Example note to product owners (email template):
Subject: Quantization drift detected on service:billing-qa — action: hybrid-shadow started
Body: We detected a -6.2% F1 drop on billing-intent slice at 2026-06-05 10:12Z. A-layer mitigations were applied automatically and reduced error by ~1%. We started hybrid-shadowing (float16 baseline + int8 candidate) at 10:35Z; divergence remains > action-threshold. We have scheduled float16 rollback for 11:05Z if divergence persists.
